title: Hubble photographs grand design spiral galaxy M81
caption: The grand design spiral galaxy Messier 81, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: Messier 81 · constellation Ursa Major · about 12 million light-years away (source figure)
credit: NASA, ESA and the Hubble Heritage Team (STScI/AURA). Acknowledgment: A. Zezas and J. Huchra (Harvard-Smithsonian Center for Astrophysics)

recognition.text: Official ESA/Hubble press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: The arms of Messier 81, a large grand design spiral galaxy, wind all the way down into its centre in this Hubble image. When it was released, it was the sharpest image ever taken of this galaxy.
A grand design spiral has long, well-defined arms that sweep neatly around the galaxy. Messier 81 is a spiral of stars, dust and clouds of gas, and it lies 11.6 million light-years away.

Even at that distance, Hubble's view is sharp enough to pick out individual stars. It also resolves open star clusters, which are loose groups of young stars, and globular clusters, which are dense balls of old stars. It even shows glowing patches of fluorescent gas, lit up by nearby stars. Hubble built it from blue, visible and infrared light.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (18.85 x 12.67 arcminutes) and distance (12 million light years), the frame spans roughly 66,000 × 44,000 light-years. Its light set out about 12 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This colour composite comes from Hubble's Advanced Camera for Surveys, assembled from images in blue, visible and near-infrared light. The source does not publish which colour was assigned to each filter.
understand.eye: The near-infrared part of the data is invisible to the eye, and no eye could separate the individual stars of a galaxy this far away.

explore: The picture was first presented at a meeting of the American Astronomical Society in Honolulu, Hawaii. Messier 81 lies in the constellation Ursa Major.
alt: A large spiral galaxy whose arms wind down into a bright core.
